title: The Great Generational Wealth Divide — TikTok
notes: Story: Boomers hold the wealth, Millennials the debt → the baby boom → they ran Congress and wrote the rules → housing → the debt landed on younger generations → the $84T handoff is concentrated at the top → what would help.
All figures are from the article (Mar 18, 2026). Where the article names a source it's shown on screen; otherwise the article itself is credited.
Photos: Wikimedia Commons. Clips: Pixabay. Credits print on screen and are listed in credits.md.

post.caption: Boomers own about half of America's wealth. Millennials hold almost half its debt. How did one generation end up with so much, and what happens to the $84 trillion they're about to pass down?

headline.text: Boomers own half of America's wealth.

say: Baby Boomers own about half of all the wealth in America.
Millennials, on the other hand, hold almost half of the debt.
We looked at how that happened, starting with the baby boom.

scenes.query: Children of the United States in the 1950s
say: Between 1946 and 1964, seventy-six million babies were born in the U.S.
California was building a new school every week to keep up.
In 1976 the first Boomers could run for Congress, and by 2013 they held sixty percent of it.

scenes.source: Generation Distribution of Congress · American Inequality
say: That was with only a quarter of the population, and they still hold 228 seats.

scenes.title: The rules they wrote
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Those lawmakers limited new housing, wrote tax rules that favored wealth, and protected retirement benefits.

overlays.label: of all U.S. real estate wealth is owned by Boomers

say: Boomers now own forty-one percent of real estate wealth, often in big homes with few people in them.

scenes.title: New homes with 4+ bedrooms
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: In the seventies one in five new homes had four bedrooms or more, and now it's nearly half.

scenes.title: Share of all U.S. debt
say: Younger generations got the debt instead, and Millennials now hold forty-one percent of it.

stats.label: held by the top 10% of Boomers

scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Now eighty-four trillion dollars is being passed down, and the top ten percent of Boomers hold seventy-one percent of it.
Sharing it more widely means more housing, affordable college, and higher wages.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
